about.title: East Palo Alto Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: East Palo Alto sees a steady share of injury collisions each year, with public records showing 112 injury crashes and 163 people hurt in the most recent reporting year alone. Corridors like University Avenue, E Bayshore Road, Bay Road, and the US-101 interchanges carry heavy commuter and local traffic, and reported collisions tend to cluster on Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. when the roads are busiest. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the days right after matter: photos, witness contact information, and medical records can fade or disappear fast. Our team handles personal injury claims in San Mateo County. There's no cost to talk, and no fee owed unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why East Palo Alto Residents Choose Us

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting early preserves your options.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Clear-Cut
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for the crash. We can help make sure shared fault doesn't unfairly shrink your claim.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and we work on contingency — no fee unless you win.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on US-101 or a road maintained by a government agency?
items.answer: Claims involving government-owned roads or vehicles come with a much shorter filing deadline, sometimes as little as six months instead of two years. Because East Palo Alto sits along several state and county-maintained corridors, it's worth having this checked quickly.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free case review, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your case results in a recovery. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with us.
